title: Chole Masala

items: 1-1.5 cup reserved water from the pressure cooker

method: The next day, pressure cook the chickpeas in the black tea + water , i do it for 6-7 whistles because i like slightly mushy and very well cooked chickpeas ( i prefer it as it doesn’t give me acidity that way ) but if you prefer you can do 4-5 whistles
Once done, let the pressure aside and drain the chickpeas ensuring you retain the water for use later
Roast all the spices in a pan till fragrant and let it cool
Pulse in the mixie till you get a fine powder
Add oil to the pan then add in onions and ginger garlic paste
Let it cook then add in tomatoes and saute for a few minutes
Add in the chole masala along with the other spice powders and the slit green chillies and saute again
Add in the chickpeas coat them well in the masala and add in reserve water
Want a thick gravy? simmer it open for 10 minutes
Want a thinner gravy? simmer it covered for 10 minutes
Once its cooked, top with coriander and thin slices of ginger ( if you want )
Serve with roti/rice as you like it :)
Tastes great with kachumber on the side

Chole Masala
Home Food 101 | Vegan | | Lunch Box 

Nutrition: 
C: 46 | F: 5 | P: 15
Calories: 287 per serve 
Serves 4

Ingredients
1 cup chickpeas, uncooked, around 190 grams 
1 cup black tea brewed
2 cups water, to pressure cook

masala 
4 black peppercorn
2 cloves
2 elaichi pods
1 inch cinnamon / 1/2 tsp cinnamon powder
1 tsp jeera
1 tsp saunf
1 tsp coriander seeds
2 kashmiri red chilli

gravy
1 tsp oil
1 onion
1 tbsp ginger garlic paste 
2 tomatoes 
1 tsp red chilli powder
1/2 tsp haldi
1 tsp coriander powder
2 green chillies, split
1-1.5 cup reserved water from the pressure cooker
1 1/2 tsp aamchur powder

Method 
soak chickpeas overnight 
the next day, pressure cook the chickpeas in the black tea + water , i do it for 6-7 whistles because i like slightly mushy and very well cooked chickpeas ( i prefer it as it doesn’t give me acidity that way ) but if you prefer you can do 4-5 whistles
once done, let the pressure aside and drain the chickpeas ensuring you retain the water for use later

chole masala 
roast all the spices in a pan till fragrant and let it cool
pulse in the mixie till you get a fine powder

gravy
add oil to the pan then add in onions and ginger garlic paste
let it cook then add in tomatoes and saute for a few minutes
add in the chole masala along with the other spice powders and the slit green chillies and saute again
add in the chickpeas coat them well in the masala and add in reserve water
want a thick gravy? simmer it open for 10 minutes
want a thinner gravy? simmer it covered for 10 minutes
once its cooked, top with coriander and thin slices of ginger ( if you want ) 

serve with roti/rice as you like it :) 
tastes great with kachumber on the side
